The paper presents a method for identifying the internal structure of a multilayered particle using scattering data.
The approach involves a best fit to data functional and a combination of local and global minimization methods.
Using multiple frequencies can improve the identification of the particle's structure and reduce the number of undistinguishable configurations.
The best fit to data functional Φ measures the difference between the observed scattering data and the simulated data for a given configuration.
The Reduction Procedure reduces the dimensionality of the minimization space by replacing two adjacent layers with one occupying their place.
The Local Minimization Method (LMM) combines the Basic Minimization Method and the Reduction Procedure to find a local minimum in a lower-dimensional subspace.
The Hybrid Stochastic-Deterministic Method combines a global search with a local minimization, developed in [15] for the identification of small subsurface particles.
The dimension of the minimization space is chosen to be larger than 2N, where N is the unknown number of layers in the original scatterer.
The stopping criterion in the Basic Minimization Method determines when to stop the minimization process and consider the current configuration as a local minimum.
The simulated annealing method is a probabilistic global minimization method that uses a temperature schedule to control the exploration of the search space.
The TRUST method is a global minimization method that uses a trust region to control the exploration of the search space.
The interval method is a global minimization method that uses intervals to represent the search space and iteratively narrows down the intervals to find a global minimum.
The three free space wavenumbers chosen to be used in the multifrequency approach are 3.0, 6.5, and 10.0.
The best fit profile for the configuration qr exhibits a sharp minimum at r = 0.4.
The value of the best fit to data functional Φ at the configuration Q2 is 0.00012.
The value of the best fit to data functional Φ at the configuration Q2 when the free space wavenumber k is equal to 10.0 is 1.4307.
